marrow__PHYSIO_CH37_Q019.takeaway: Thyroxine-binding globulin carries the largest share of circulating T4 with high affinity.
marrow__PHYSIO_CH37_Q019.displayText:
Thyroxine-binding globulin carries the largest share of circulating T4 with high affinity.

Thyroxine-binding globulin (TBG) is the major thyroxine-binding protein.
Other thyroxine-binding proteins are:
• Albumin
• Transthyretin (TTR)/ thyroxine-binding pre-albumin (TBPA)
• Lipoproteins
emphasis: Thyroxine-binding globulin carries the largest share of circulating T4 with high affinity

rationales.a: Albumin binds thyroid hormone but has lower affinity and is not the main carrier.
rationales.b: Transthyretin carries some T4, particularly in cerebrospinal fluid, but less than TBG.
rationales.d: Transferrin transports iron, not the main thyroid-hormone carrier.

marrow__PHYSIO_CH37_Q020.takeaway: T4 has a longer plasma half-life than T3; T3 is more potent and binds nuclear receptors more avidly.
marrow__PHYSIO_CH37_Q020.displayText:
T4 has a longer plasma half-life than T3; T3 is more potent and binds nuclear receptors more avidly.

T4 doesn't have a shorter half-life than T3, rather T3 has a shorter half-life and more rapid action than T4.
The table compares T4 and T3:
emphasis: T4 has a longer plasma half-life than T3; T3 is more potent and binds nuclear receptors more avidly

rationales.a: T3 binds thyroid hormone receptors more avidly, so this is true.
rationales.b: T4 circulates at higher concentration than T3, so this is true.
rationales.c: T3 is the more biologically active hormone, so this is true.

marrow__PHYSIO_CH37_Q021.takeaway: T4 has a plasma half-life of roughly 6–7 days, longer than T3’s.
marrow__PHYSIO_CH37_Q021.displayText:
T4 has a plasma half-life of roughly 6–7 days, longer than T3’s.

The half-life of T4 is 6 - 7 days.
T3 has the shorter half-life of 1 day.
emphasis: T4 has a plasma half-life of roughly 6–7 days, longer than T3’s

rationales.a: Ten hours is much shorter than the T4 half-life.
rationales.c: Six weeks is too long for the circulating T4 half-life.
rationales.d: Two to three months exceeds the expected T4 half-life.

marrow__PHYSIO_CH37_Q022.takeaway: Thyrotoxicosis raises heart rate/stroke volume and lowers peripheral resistance; protein breakdown increases, so decreased breakdown is absent.
marrow__PHYSIO_CH37_Q022.displayText:
Thyrotoxicosis raises heart rate/stroke volume and lowers peripheral resistance; protein breakdown increases, so decreased breakdown is absent.

The given clinical scenario is suggestive of hyperthyroidism, which does not cause decreased protein breakdown. Rather it causes increased protein breakdown.
emphasis: Thyrotoxicosis raises heart rate/stroke volume and lowers peripheral resistance; protein breakdown increases, so decreased breakdown is absent

rationales.a: Thyroid hormone increases heart rate and cardiac output.
rationales.b: Stroke volume and cardiac output generally rise in thyrotoxicosis.
rationales.c: Peripheral vascular resistance falls with increased tissue heat production and vasodilation.

marrow__PHYSIO_CH37_Q023.takeaway: Prolactin is high immediately after delivery and during lactation, with suckling sustaining its secretion.
marrow__PHYSIO_CH37_Q023.displayText:
Prolactin is high immediately after delivery and during lactation, with suckling sustaining its secretion.

Among the given options, the prolactin level is highest 24 hours after delivery.
The maximum level of prolactin is seen during pregnancy and in the immediate postpartum period. During pregnancy, the secretion is increased reaching a peak at the time of delivery. After delivery, the plasma concentration falls to nonpregnant levels in a few weeks. Suckling produces surges of prolactin release.
emphasis: Prolactin is high immediately after delivery and during lactation, with suckling sustaining its secretion

rationales.a: Ovulation is not the time of maximal prolactin secretion.
rationales.c: Sleep can raise prolactin, but the postpartum/lactation state has the high level asked here.
rationales.d: Exercise may alter prolactin modestly but is not its peak condition.

marrow__PHYSIO_CH37_Q024.takeaway: Cushing disease (pituitary ACTH adenoma) produces elevated ACTH and cortisol due to ACTH-driven adrenal stimulation.
marrow__PHYSIO_CH37_Q024.displayText:
Cushing disease (pituitary ACTH adenoma) produces elevated ACTH and cortisol due to ACTH-driven adrenal stimulation.

Among the given conditions, the levels of ACTH and cortisol will be highest in Cushing's disease.
Cushing's disease is caused by an ACTH secreting pituitary adenoma. The increased ACTH causes increased cortisol production.
Note: In normal physiologic state, ACTH levels are higher in the early morning but not as high as in Cushing's disease.
emphasis: Cushing disease (pituitary ACTH adenoma) produces elevated ACTH and cortisol due to ACTH-driven adrenal stimulation

rationales.a: Morning is a normal circadian peak but below pathologic Cushing levels.
rationales.b: Dexamethasone suppresses ACTH/cortisol in normal individuals.
rationales.c: Addison disease raises ACTH but cortisol is low, so both are not high.
